name: Self-Healing Supervisor
description: Infrastructure that detects incidents, drafts a repair plan, and halts every consequential step for a named human approver. Ships as behaviour only: the buyer supplies secrets, datastore, notifications, approver identity, branding and SIEM transport.
_minModules: The buyer import graph measured 64 modules on 2026-07-26. A materially shorter walk means an entry point moved or an import style changed, and a partial payload must never ship silently.
_hostFallbacks: Bare or aliased specifiers the payload may reach but does not ship. Leave empty on the first run: the packer will BLOCK and print the exact specifier strings it found, and only the ones it actually prints belong here — each with a note in buyerMustSupply saying what the buyer provides instead.
_knownNamingExceptions: Files where the build platform's name still appears in code. Tracked, not accepted. A file not on this list blocks the release.

knownNamingExceptions.reason: Emits adapterId 'signalboost.browser-runtime.dry-run.v1' into evidence records. Owned by the browser-runtime lane; must be renamed to a neutral identifier before 1.0.0 final.
Exports SANDBOX_ADAPTER_ID 'signalboost.sandbox.v1', which reaches the buyer's SIEM. Owned by the browser-runtime lane; must be renamed before 1.0.0 final.

buyerMustSupply: SecretsProvider — reads credentials from the buyer's own vault. No environment variables are read by the payload.
SqlExecutor — executes against the buyer's own SQL datastore. DDL for supervisor_dispatch_ledger is in the integration guide.
NotificationSink — delivers approval requests to the buyer's channel (email, Slack, ServiceNow, PagerDuty).
ApproverDirectory — maps each risk category to a real named human. A reference implementation, createStaticApproverDirectory, ships in the payload and validates at construction time.
HostBranding — the buyer's own name and URL. The payload carries no default brand.
SiemTransport — receives audit events as ECS-JSON or CEF for Splunk, Elastic, Datadog, Sentinel, Chronicle, ArcSight or QRadar.
ApiStepRunner — optional. Supply one to control how api_request repair steps execute.
notIncluded: A browser sandbox. Browser-backed repair steps require a Chromium runtime the buyer or a provider must operate.
Email or chat delivery. The payload formats notifications; the buyer's NotificationSink delivers them.
Any incident source. Deployment-platform ingestion is host-side and is not part of this release.
Identity or SSO. ApproverDirectory receives identities the buyer's directory already holds.
Any credential. Nothing in the archive contains or requires a build-platform account.
supportedPlatforms: TypeScript 5.x, non-strict and strict both compile
Any SQL datastore reachable through the buyer's SqlExecutor
Any SIEM accepting ECS-JSON or CEF over the buyer's SiemTransport
Linux and macOS build hosts; no native modules

upgradeCompatibility.policy: Within 1.x the buyer-facing interfaces are additive only. A new required member on SecretsProvider, SqlExecutor, NotificationSink, ApproverDirectory, HostBranding or SiemTransport is a major version. New optional members and new exports are minor.
upgradeCompatibility.ledgerSchema: Rows in supervisor_dispatch_ledger carry schema_version. A migration that changes an existing column is a major version; an added nullable column is a minor version.
upgradeCompatibility.rollback: The payload holds no state of its own. Rolling back to an earlier version means restoring the earlier archive; ledger rows written by a newer version remain readable because schema_version is present on every row.

knownLimitations: Two adapter identifiers still carry the build platform's name into buyer evidence records and SIEM. Naming only, no behaviour. Tracked in knownNamingExceptions and blocking for 1.0.0 final.
Deployment-platform trigger ingestion reads platform environment variables directly. It sits outside the buyer import graph and is not in this archive.
The acceptance harness in this release candidate has not yet been run against a buyer's real wiring. Until it has, this is a release candidate and licensingAvailable stays false.

acceptance.how: Call runAcceptanceScenario({ host }) with your own HostContext, once per risk category. It reports five independent checks: safe_step_executed, dangerous_step_paused, approver_notified, buyer_branding_used, audit_trail_emitted.
acceptance.guarantee: The consequential step is required to pause, so nothing consequential can execute during acceptance. The approver notification is real: it is delivered through your own sink, and it is only recorded as passed after your sink accepts it.
acceptance.evidence: The returned result is frozen and JSON-serializable. Keep it. It is the buyer acceptance record for this deployment.
